direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is honestly just very bland, feeling like the direction we're seeing from a lot of BookTok movies lately, where it's just 'let's get this movie made because people are going to come watch it,' as it looks exactly like The Housemaid, down to the house, with lazy, predictable world-building and a thriller element that feels so forced; the direction on a microscale is genuinely bad, and while Michael Showalter is not a terrible director since I've seen him direct decent movies, it feels like he just wasn't in the room, as Dakota Johnson can't act, so nobody can work off of her in the scenes that revolve around her, making them boring and bad and making all the interpersonal dialogue bad; the storytelling is somewhat of a saving grace, as it actually kept me entertained the way a BookTok movie does, offering trashy entertainment that's somewhat enjoyable, like how murder podcasts keep you entertained, just in the lowest-common-denominator way; the tension is so artificially built, as the movie tries to be a psychological thriller but is so forced that it becomes laughable

performance.comments: Not bad, as she makes the most of what she can from this movie, and while she might be overacting a little in some moments, she's good in all the scenes she's in, because she's mother, she's a good actress, and she's my favorite actress

She clearly cannot act in dramatic movies and should stop doing them, since she's actually okay in comedies; she can't show emotion, so it always feels forced, she can't modulate her voice to make it interesting, and she has no charisma, making all her scenes boring, and she has no chemistry with any of the cast, including Josh Hartnett, so it feels like they cast her for her looks and not her talent (she's also a nepo baby), when there are so many better actresses who could have made something out of this role

He has the talent and shows his charisma in some moments, as he's a charismatic guy, but the material and direction were so bad that he just doesn't give a good performance in this movie, and he has no chemistry with Dakota Johnson because she can't act

cast.comments: With bad material and Dakota Johnson unable to act, nobody can work off of her, leaving the cast with little chemistry, even though Anne Hathaway makes the most of what she's given

story.comments: The concept is stupid, as it's literally BookTok: The Movie, trying to be a meta commentary on BookTok while being BookTok itself, and its love triangle makes it the exact same movie as The Housemaid, showing how unoriginal these movies are; the plot structure is actually interesting, as you're in the present day while reading the disabled author's manuscripts to jump to the past and build context for the story, but the movie has no real climax, as it's so forced and abrupt, and it tries to end on an open-ended note that is just so stupid; character writing is bad, as Dakota Johnson's character is so surface level, Anne Hathaway's Verity is set up as a villain with a twist at the end that I predicted from a mile away, and like all these BookTok movies and books, it pushes the same narrative that men seem good on the surface but are actually bad, which is just bad writing

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is genuinely bad and logically makes no sense, with so many lines that don't match what's going on or that no one would say in sequence, making it obvious they shot straight off the original script without tailoring it to the scenes; the humor is laughably bad, and the erotic moments are so forced that the movie just becomes smut, which is obviously for BookTok people; the symbolism isn't worth analyzing, as there is imagery that panders to people who are into murder podcasts, but this movie does not deserve to be analyzed; the foreshadowing is so evident because every Colleen Hoover BookTok book has the same messaging that men are not what they seem, leading to the same climax and ending, and it's a perfect example of 'I wasn't wrong, I was just early,' as the twist I predicted comes so late after the climax that they run out of room to end the movie properly

score.comments: There are moments where Volker Bertelmann shows he's a good composer, but there are a lot of moments where his style just doesn't fit the movie, making it feel like he shouldn't have taken this project, especially for someone who's won an Oscar

soundtrack.comments: A lot of BookTok-esque soundtrack songs

cinematography.comments: Bland and boring, your typical BookTok cinematography, showing they put no effort into making this movie since they knew it would make money

editing.comments: Same as the cinematography, with a lot of bad editing sequences and cuts that just aren't well cut

sound.comments: So artificial in how it tries to create tension in the erotic and psychological thriller moments, making it obvious how they force it

production_design.comments: Set in a nice house and in Vermont, but every BookTok movie looks the same, and that shows through the production design

makeup.comments: Everyone in this movie is hot, and they try to make Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson, and Josh Hartnett all look hot, which kind of aids the movie

costumes.comments: I might be dumb, but they try to show Dakota Johnson wearing the same dress as Anne Hathaway, and it looks like two different dresses

review.pacing: Actually not that bad for how much plot there is, as you are entertained throughout the whole movie, and the way it's structured, going back and forth to give you context, keeps it from ever feeling like it drags that much
review.climax: Not executed well, as it's genuinely very anticlimactic and stupid, and the twist I predicted comes so late that the movie can't end properly and feels like it ran out of space; the runtime is fine, but cutting some scenes in the middle would have made for a stronger ending
review.tone: Feels very much like a bland, boring BookTok movie that panders to the lowest common denominator, people who have never read a serious book in their life, looking so lazy because they knew BookTok would make it the easiest cash grab ever; at its core, it's an erotic psychological thriller, just a very cheaply made and lazily put together one
review.final_notes: At my screening at AMC Techridge, to the right of me were two BookTok girls who were giddy and surprised the whole time because it's very obvious they've never read a serious book in their life, and to the left of me were two guys who were audible during the intimate scenes and whenever anyone was naked, so I was in between both target demographics for this movie
review.overall: Overall, 'Verity' is an entertaining movie, but it's also not a good one; at the end of the day, this movie has bad material, panders to the lowest common denominator, and is led by Dakota Johnson, who genuinely cannot act, setting it up to fail big time; the many flaws in the direction and writing make it so obvious that they lazily put this movie together because they knew they were going to milk money off of the main demographic for this movie: BookTokers who clearly have never read a serious book in their lives
